newsitem.title: UK: RRNE IN TALKS WITH TRAIN DRIVERS, HOPEFUL OF DEAL.
newsitem.headline: RRNE IN TALKS WITH TRAIN DRIVERS, HOPEFUL OF DEAL.

text.p: Britain's Regional Railways North East (RRNE), whose drivers voted in favour of strike action earlier on Tuesday, said it was locked in talks with union leaders to resolve the issue.
It was hopeful of a resolution to avoid a strike.

"We have been speaking to Aslef (the train drivers' union) since yesterday (Monday) morning. The talks were positive and are continuing today. We are totally committed to resolving this issue before it reaches the stage of industrial action," spokesman Bill Hearld said.
Almost all of RRNE's 700 drivers are Aslef (Associated Society of locomotive Engineers and Firemen) members.
The talks were due to end later on Tuesday. RRNE said it hoped to have some sort of agreement by then.
"It would be nice if we could. We hope to make this strike ballot result redundant," said Hearld.
He added that Aslef representatives had outlined their demands and a deal was currently under discussion which would give drivers more days off in return for greater flexibility in rostas.
Aslef said earlier its members had voted for a series of 24-hour strikes and a ban on overtime.
"This vote for industrial action underlines the importance of safeguarding quality time off for train drivers," ASLEF general secretary Lew Adams said in a statement.
RRNE is owned by MTL Rail Ltd, a division of MTL Trust Holdings, the Liverpool-based transport group.

The RRNE rail franchise runs train services in north-east England, running from the Scottish border to South Yorkshire and covering major northern cities including Manchester, Liverpool, Newcastle and Blackpool.
Adams said the drivers voted to strike because, they claimed, RRNE had failed to keep an agreement which allowed drivers to work 37-hour weeks.
But he said he was optimistic that the dispute could be resolved without implementing the series of strikes and overtime ban.
"The ball is definitely in RRNE's court, and we expect the company to deliver the quality time off to which our drivers are entitled," Adams added.
